title: Self-limiting electrostriction of a single ion in an ultracold polar gas: From mesoscopic ions to crystalline molecular rings
authors: Ruiren Shi, Saajid Chowdhury, Leon Karpa, Jesús Pérez-Ríos
abstract: We investigate the self-assembly of polar molecules around a single ion immersed in an ultracold, dilute two-dimensional molecular gas. The ion aligns and attracts the molecules through charge-dipole interactions, producing a strong electrostrictive accumulation around the impurity, while intermolecular repulsion limits further densification and favors spatially extended configurations. By combining global optimization with diffusion Monte Carlo, we calculate the evaporation energy as a function of the number of molecules bound to the ion. In contrast to conventional charged and van der Waals clusters, the evaporation energy exhibits a plateau-like dependence on cluster size, reflecting the sequential formation of concentric molecular rings. These structures are governed by the topology of the ion's electric field and by the competition between attractive ion-molecule interactions, repulsive intra-ring interactions, and attractive correlations between neighboring rings, rather than by conventional coordination or icosahedral packing. In the weak-interaction regime, the resulting structures form extended mesoscopic molecular ions, whereas stronger interactions produce increasingly rigid, crystal-like molecular rings. We further analyze their stability against thermal perturbations and the time-dependent ion trap and find that a broad range of clusters remain stable under experimentally relevant conditions. The intermolecular repulsion and dipolar geometry also suppress close-range ion-molecule encounters, suggesting an intrinsic shielding mechanism. Our results establish ion-bound polar-molecule clusters as a distinct class of mesoscopic molecular ions and open a route to studying charged impurities in quantum baths with anisotropic interactions.
summary: This paper models the self-assembly of polar molecules around an ion in an ultracold 2D gas, driven by electrostriction. The authors find that the resulting clusters form distinct, concentric molecular rings whose stability is dictated by the electric field topology rather than simple packing rules. This establishes a new theoretical framework for understanding charged impurities in quantum molecular baths.
main_problem: The study investigates the self-assembly and structural evolution of polar molecules surrounding a single ion immersed in an ultracold, dilute two-dimensional molecular gas.
main_result: The system forms concentric molecular rings whose structure is governed by the ion's electric field topology, establishing a new class of mesoscopic molecular ions stabilized by self-limiting electrostriction.
method: The research combines global optimization with Diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations to determine the evaporation energy as a function of cluster size.
model_or_system: The system consists of an ion interacting with polar molecules via anisotropic charge-dipole and dipole-dipole interactions in a 2D gas. The physics is governed by the competition between attractive ion-molecule forces and repulsive intra-ring interactions.
key_observables: Evaporation energy as a function of the number of bound molecules, and the resulting molecular cluster structure (mesoscopic ion vs. crystalline ring).
important_parameters: The strength of the dipole-dipole interaction, the dimensionality (2D), and the regime of interaction (weak vs. strong).
main_assumptions: Assumes molecules are rigid rotors and that the dipole moments align with the local electric field for force calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the Stark manifold, the 2D system setup, and the nature of the ion-dipole and dipole-dipole interactions. Figure 2 likely shows the calculated evaporation energy versus the number of molecules.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the physical model and Hamiltonian, detailing the computational methods (DMC, optimization), presenting the key results regarding the plateau-like evaporation energy, and concluding with the physical interpretation of the resulting molecular structures.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physics of charged impurities in quantum baths, utilizing anisotropic dipolar interactions which are central to modern AMO research involving polar molecules and trapped ions.
